s1.syndrome_frame: Abdominal mass with chronic vomiting and right upper-quadrant pain
salient_findings: Large, firm, palpable mass in the right upper quadrant
Large retroperitoneal mass with fatty and soft-tissue components
key_facts: 2-year history of intermittent vomiting
Right upper-quadrant pain
Sensation of fullness on the right side of the abdomen
Denies urinary symptoms or changes in bowel habits
History of heavy menstruation and iron deficiency anemia
Oral iron therapy for over 10 years
Beta-thalassemia trait on hemoglobin electrophoresis
Hemoglobin levels ranging from 6 to 10 g/dL
Abdominal ultrasonography showed a well-defined hyperechoic heterogeneous mass
Contrast-enhanced CT showed a well-defined, encapsulated retroperitoneal lesion
MRI confirmed a large right retroperitoneal predominantly fatty mass

shortlist.label: Myelolipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Large right retroperitoneal predominantly fatty mass with soft-tissue nodular and linear strand-like areas

shortlist.label: Adrenal myelolipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Location of the mass in the right adrenal gland area and presence of fatty tissue

shortlist.label: Retroperitoneal lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Well-defined hyperechoic heterogeneous mass with minimal vascularity and mostly fat density

shortlist.label: Liposarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Large size of the mass and presence of soft-tissue density areas within the fatty mass

shortlist.label: Retroperitoneal teratoma
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of a large, complex mass with both fatty and soft-tissue components

raw.rationale: The presence of a large, well-defined, encapsulated retroperitoneal lesion with mostly fat density and internal areas of soft-tissue density, as seen on CT and MRI, is consistent with myelolipoma. The location in the hepatorenal space, near the right adrenal gland, and the absence of invasion into adjacent organs support this diagnosis. The patient's long-standing anemia and beta-thalassemia trait may also be related to the myeloid component of the tumor.

rejected.label: Myelolipoma
rejected.why: Too general, as myelolipoma can occur in other locations

rejected.label: Retroperitoneal lipoma
rejected.why: Lack of soft-tissue components and myeloid elements

rejected.label: Liposarcoma
rejected.why: Typically shows more aggressive features and invasion into adjacent organs

rejected.label: Retroperitoneal teratoma
rejected.why: Usually contains multiple tissue types, including cystic components, and is less likely to be predominantly fatty
